candidate.title: MAINE-Seq/Mnase-Seq/Nucleo-Seq
candidate.scope: Shared explanatory architecture targeted by the assigned MAINE-Seq/Mnase-Seq/Nucleo-Seq card: open nucleosomal chromatin is digested with MNase, trimmed DNA-protein complexes are recovered, and their DNA is extracted. The drawing calls MAINE-Seq and MNase-Seq corresponding names; Nucleo-Seq is retained as a card-level target with its own paper association, not asserted to be an identical complete protocol. The left yellow-accented nucleosome icon accompanies the naming caption, has no transformation arrow and no modification legend, and is not a separate preparation. All workflow arrows form one route; the two isolated particle views are not branches. The depicted endpoint is DNA. Catalogue and paper text explain its downstream library/readout interface, without adding unshown library operations, end chemistry, size-selection procedures, or sequencing settings.

operations.label: MNase digestion
operations.description: Cut exposed DNA in the starting nucleosomal chromatin, converting linked chromatin into a digest containing trimmed DNA-protein complexes. The retained route follows protected DNA; removed exposed DNA is not drawn as a separate recovered product.
operations.mechanism: Micrococcal nuclease cleaves accessible DNA while nucleosomes and other DNA-bound obstructions can protect segments. Orange circles occur in the digestion panel, but no tethered nuclease, covalent label or additional biological input is specified.
operations.information_effect: Chromatin protection is converted into a distribution of surviving genomic DNA fragments. Their positions support nucleosome occupancy/position mapping, subject to digestion and representation biases; protection alone does not identify the protecting protein.
